# Address index

Address -> the documents that cite it. Ghidra image base `0x00120000`.

**GENERATED — do not hand-edit.** `Tools/analysis-kit/gfz-scripts/gen_address_index.py`

This file was hand-maintained and held **74 addresses** while the database cited
**19604 distinct functions across 524 documents** — about 1 % coverage, with none of the
documents written on 2026-09-03 appearing at all. Its own header had said to generate
it *"once enough documents exist"*, and that threshold passed unnoticed.

> **A hand-maintained index two orders of magnitude behind is worse than no index: a
> reader who looks up an address and finds nothing concludes the database does not
> cover it.**

**Interior addresses resolve to their containing function**, so a citation of an
instruction indexes under the function it is in. **It does not name functions** — the
ledger's names are mechanical for most of these, and a generated index asserting a name
would assert something no document said. This answers *who talks about this address*
and nothing else.

**19604 addresses cited by a document · 9219 by more than one.**

**A further 14158 addresses are recorded only in a `.tsv` side file** and are listed below the main table, marked `table only`. **A table row is a transcription, not an explanation** — it makes the address findable and asserts nothing about whether the database understands it. They are deliberately *not* counted as cited.
